data.name: Anvika
data.gender_notes: Anvika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anvika is derived from the Sanskrit words 'anu' meaning 'with' and 'vika' meaning 'knowledge'. The name symbolizes the graceful and beautiful being who is rich in knowledge and wisdom. The name Anvika carries the meaning “Graceful, Beautiful, Knowledgeable” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anvika usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, beautiful, knowledgeable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Anvika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful, Beautiful, Knowledgeable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anvika total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Anvika is mentioned as the name of a queen in the epic Mahabharata. She was the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandavas and Kauravas. Anvika is also known as Amba, and her story involves her unrequited love for Bhishma.

Anvika is also the name of a goddess in Hinduism, particularly worshipped in the state of Karnataka (south India). The goddess is believed to be a form of Parvati, the consort of Shiva, and is associated with love, fertility, and protection.
